TSE is a homology-dependent mechanism which can be triggered by a sequence exogenous (here lacZ) to the D. melangaster genome.
the telomeric silencing of P elements is a homology-dependent mechanism that can be induced via sequences that do not belong to the Drosophil melanogaster genome.
the trans-silenced state can be induced by a telomeric P element in a target locus sharing solely a sequence exogenouse to D. melanogasters genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of transposons and their interactions with the host genome.
understanding how the piRNA pathway is involved in the silencing of P elements.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of transposable elements in Drosophilla.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TSE is a homology-dependent mechanism that can be induced when the silencer and target sequences share homology with a transposon, but also when they share solely homology with a sequence exogenous of the D. melanogastrer genome.
the piRNA pathway is involved in the silencing of P-elements in the germlines of both D. melanogaste and D. simulans.
TSE represents the most general form of silencing in the germlines of Drosophila species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TSE is a homology-dependent, epigenetic, maternal effect and germline-specific repression mechanism that can be induced by a telomeric P-element and by the exogenous lacZ gene.
the TSE mechanism can be triggered by the presence of a telomeric P element in the germlines of females and that it can also be triggered by other sequences exogenous to Drosophila genome.
the piRNA pathway, a germline-specific silencing mechanism, can be used in a trans-generational fashion to repress a transgene inserted in the genome of D. melanogasters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TSE can be used to repress a transgene by homology to an exogenous sequence, in the Drosphila germline.
a transposable element can silence another transposable element by using only sequences that are foreign to the genome of the host.
TSE is not restricted to the P element family, but can be induced via homology with any sequence exogenous to D. melanogastersuch as lacZ.
